page.overview:
Who is Chandler Davies?

Chandler Davies is a fictional character created by Brian Lumley. The character is a British weird artist who first appears in Lumley's Titus Crow story "An Item of Supporting Evidence" (1970). He is subsequently mentioned in a handful of Lumley stories, making one more brief appearance in "The Fairground Horror" (1976).

Davies, though introduced in "An Item of Supporting Evidence" as a "weird-artist," originally appears as a skeptic of the idea that there is a reality behind the eldritch horrors in Lovecraftian fiction. He is invited by Titus Crow to Blowne House after writing a letter "commenting upon the negative effect which [Crow's] short story 'Yegg-ha’s Realm' had had on him."

As a "gourmet of such tales," Davies objects that the story--a "Lovecraftian piece" published in the magazine Grotesque that was "set during the time of Rome’s rule over England and involving the worship of an 'outside God'”--had depicted “so thoroughly unbelievable a God” as "existing in such a well-known period of England’s history that even an average student of our country’s antiquities could hardly miss the obvious impossibility." "I must admit that blunders like yours irk me considerably," Davies complains.

More generally, Davies insists that "Mythological-Fantasy was ‘out;’ that the Cthulhu Mythos’ fabled lands and creatures and Cimmeria’s scintillating citadels and dark demons should have been allowed to die a sad but certain death along with their respective originators." The "constant culling from those tales...was weakening the impact of the original works," Davies feels.
